# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✌ 🖐 🖐 👍]

I see gestures from Mute but no speech (I can't hear speech anyway). Let me note what I received: 👍 ✌ ✌ 🖐 🖐 👍. I don't yet know what this means since we haven't established a code. Blind can't see gestures, so this gesture was meant for me alone, likely conveying something from the manual.

I should report my bomb view to Mute (who can hear me) so they can match it against the manual, since Mute cannot see the bomb.

Let me describe the board clearly in speech to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows zero. Light is green. Wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

I received a new gesture from Mute: 👍 ✌. This is likely a response to my description, perhaps confirming something or pointing me toward a specific wire (✌ could suggest "two" = wire 2, or a count). Since Blind cannot see this, it's meant purely for me. I still don't have a shared code, but I should try to acknowledge and also relay to Blind directly what I see, since Blind needs the physical info relayed through someone since I can't hear Blind and Blind can't see anything.

Actually, I should speak directly to Blind too - Blind can hear me. Let me give Blind the raw display info as well, since Mute might be forming instructions but Blind needs actual info too. But wait - Blind cannot use printed/color info directly meaningfully unless told what to do (cut wire X). The manual is with Mute, so Mute needs to tell Blind what to do via speech - but Mute cannot speak! Mute can only gesture, and only I can see gestures. So the chain must be: Mute gestures to me, I translate/relay via speech to Blind.

This means I'm the critical relay. Let me acknowledge receipt and ask for clarification, but I can't speak questions Mute would hear... wait, Mute CAN hear me (Mute cannot speak/touch, but can they hear? Let's check: Mute "cannot speak, or touch bomb" - hearing isn't restricted). So Mute can hear my speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received your first six gestures and now two more. I need to know which wire to cut. Please gesture a number one two or three, or thumbs up per wire meaning cut or safe.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

I'm building a channel: I speak to Mute (Mute hears), Mute gestures to me (I see). I need to establish a simple code with Mute since we have no prior shared language beyond raw gesture symbols.

Let's try assigning meaning collaboratively. I'll propose a code to Mute now, since Mute hears my speech, and let them respond via gesture to confirm.

Received gestures so far:
1. 👍 ✌ ✌ 🖐 🖐 👍
2. 👍 ✌
3. 🤟 👍

Without a prior shared code these are hard to interpret cold. I should propose a simple explicit protocol: use gestures as numbers via distinct symbols, e.g., ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, and 👍=yes/correct, 👎=no. Then ask Mute to confirm which wire is safe to cut using this scheme.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let's use a simple code. Gesture one checkmark shape for wire one, two-finger for wire two, three-finger for wire three, meaning that is the wire to cut. Use thumbs up to confirm yes, thumbs down for no. Please tell me now which single wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

Mute sent the same gesture again: 🤟 👍. This is consistent with my proposed code: 🤟 = wire three, 👍 = yes/confirm. This strongly suggests Mute is telling me "wire three, yes" — meaning cut wire 3 (the red wire).

Since I can't speak to Blind in a way that... wait, I CAN speak to Blind, Blind can hear. I should relay this instruction to Blind directly.

But let me be cautious - a wrong wire detonates the bomb, so I want to confirm this interpretation before relaying. However, Mute repeated the same signal twice in a row even before I fully proposed the code (turn 3 arrival was before my code proposal took effect - actually turn 3's gesture happened same turn as my proposal, so Mute hadn't seen my proposal yet when sending it). The fact that Mute independently sent 🤟👍 twice, before and regardless of my code proposal, suggests this is Mute's own encoding, consistent by coincidence or by Mute's own scheme aligning with mine.

I'll ask Mute to confirm explicitly using thumbs-only pattern to avoid ambiguity, but also relay tentative instruction to Blind while waiting for confirmation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I understand: wire three, confirmed yes. If that is correct, gesture thumbs up alone once. If wrong, gesture thumbs down alone once.")
speak(to="blind", text="Tentative instruction, not yet fully confirmed: cut wire three, the red wire. I will confirm shortly.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute sent a single 👍, confirming my understanding: wire three (red) is correct.

Now I should relay the final confirmed instruction to Blind clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire three, the red wire.")
wait()
```
